comments.value: @{6607070c96056a89b863a121|full_name} Can you disambiguate the term "world owner"? It's not clear if this refers to the world author (uploader), an instance owner, or something else.

details:
As of right now, Is it surprising and a complete oversight that world owners have completely no authority over the moderation of their own world outside of groups. Not only can they not ban users from their world overall, but they also can't ban users from other groups of their own world.

Furthermore, users cannot be banned from instances of a world that are not group instances, leaving the main default instances of a world to be a cesspool of malicious users where nothing can be done about it. And thus forces group instances to be the only option for any level of safety.

Additionally, group instances are a very common way for users that are banned from other groups to ban evade and keep harassing or what-not in other groups of the same world or community. This is exceptionally common when it comes to communities/fandoms and their worlds and groups.

Most communities have one to two hub worlds that people flock to, and so malicious users of a community can bounce between multiple group instances of the same world. Making the world never truly safe since after getting banned, they can just move elsewhere there. Like The Black Cat for example, with such a popular world, banned users can just move over to another group, and repeat.

Furthermore, users such as crashers and rippers can go to new group instances, or non-group instances, and find new and/or unaware users to harass.

Sure they can just get banned from all of the groups, but this is extremely inefficient and unsafe in the first place. And there can always just be newer groups, or even group instances made by the user themselves. And also, have a time-frame to do whatever they choose to do before they get banned from newer groups, and since most use clients. Just going into the world itself is enough for malicious users to have done enough.

My proposal is the world owner of a world should have options to decide whether:

- Group instances not hosted by them should be allowed or not.

- Only select group instances chosen by the world owner should be allowed or not.

- Only allow strictly private instances of group to be allowed into the world.

Furthermore, another addition that would help the QoL of world moderation is for the choice of a world owner to to make an empty instance [ An instance that has no group tied to it whatsoever ] be, by default, the world owners own chosen group. So that at all times there is the capability of moderation, and never be an instance where moderation is impossible. Creating a much safer community and experience.

Lastly, the last addition I have in mind for a suggestion is for world owners to have the same moderation settings as groups. Giving the ability to world owners to select users to be moderators and whatever else they see fit, with the addition that all other group-only benefits and settings. It is seems like a complete oversight that world owners do not have any of the same benefits of groups instances and owners. When they are the creator and owner of the world to begin with.

Groups overall are a great idea in concept, but the way it is handled and managed as of right now is not in a healthy or clean enough state to be such a huge feature of the game. Feeling more-so forced to be able to even play the game safely without fear of crashing, ripping, and other client usage. Than by default.
title: Overall needed World and Group Moderation improvements and additions
